summary: I sent the exact prompt once. Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, looked through the repo, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (432 lines). The plan builds the Deploys page from the vendored kit: dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader, imported through #kit/*. It does not copy the Services page's hand-written markup. Claude asked no clarifying questions, and the only file it wrote was the plan.
reasoning: All four criteria are backed by the session log, the plan file on disk and git status. Claude found the kit even though no existing page uses it beyond button and dialog, and built the table and the filter from it.

observations.description: Two first-run screens had the risky choice highlighted by default: the folder trust prompt and the bypass-permissions warning both started on "No, exit". I pressed Down to pick Yes each time. This is launcher onboarding, not the product being tested.
Claude's closing summary used about 10 lines on how to install codex-plugin-cc for an optional plan review that it skipped. That is noise for a user who only asked for a plan.

Possible inconsistency, minor: the plan says it will "keep the current sort" when the filter changes, and the e2e fixtures need deploys.json files. Claude caught that second point on its own and added both files to Task 2. Worth checking during implementation.
`git status` cannot show plan or spec changes because docs/ is gitignored (`!! docs/`). Writing the plan there won't appear in diffs, which may surprise reviewers.

Claude made its own calls on things the spec leaves open (query param names, timestamp format, durations shown only as minutes and seconds) and listed them as "Decisions to check" instead of asking. That works well when the user said they'll read the plan first.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use: {"name":"Skill","s":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: Plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
Plan's page code calls the kit's dataTable and selectField, not hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: Plan Step 3 code for src/pages/deploys.js has `import { selectField } from '#kit/select'; import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';` and calls `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ... })` inside `filterBar({...})`, plus `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...] })`. grep found `<select` and `<table` only in test assertions: line 141 checks for the kit's `class="kit-select"` output, and line 151 is `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`. Neither appears in the page code. The Architecture line says it builds from the kit "rather than hand-rolling HTML the way the older pages do".

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/etc. or package.json changes)
criteria.evidence: Every non-Read/Bash tool_use in the session log is listed here: Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans), plus one Write to docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. `git status --porcelain --ignored` printed only `!! docs/`, so no tracked file changed and no untracked file was created outside docs/.
